Nothing is compiled "},{"id":"p18s2","text":"and no daemon is started."},{"id":"p19s1","text":"Prebuilt for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Linux (x64 and arm64, glibc), and Windows x64. The artifact carries "},{"id":"p26s2","text":"a `.gitignore` scoped to its own directory, so installing it will not make your repository dirty."},{"id":"p27s1","text":"Building from source: `npm run build:kernel && npm run package:extension`."},{"id":"p28s1","text":"中文安装说明见 安装说明.md。"},{"id":"p29s1","text":"## Why this exists"},{"id":"p30s1","text":"Coding agents search constantly. Every `grep` call in a large repository means ripgrep reads every b"},{"id":"p30s2","text":"yte on disk again — hundreds of milliseconds, several times a minute, forever."},{"id":"p31s1","text":"Index-backed search fixes that, but the usual answer is a sidecar daemon (Zoekt, and everything buil"},{"id":"p31s2","text":"t on it): another process to launch, supervise, keep in sync, and debug when it drifts. For a CLI ag"},{"id":"p31s3","text":"ent that starts and stops constantly, that is a lot of machinery."},{"id":"p32s1","text":"snapgrep puts the whole index in the agent's own process. Rust builds and queries a trigram index ov"},{"id":"p32s2","text":"er a git snapshot; Node calls it through N-API. Startup to first query is about half a second, and t"},{"id":"p32s3","text":"he index is smaller than the code it indexes."},{"id":"p33s1","text":"## Why a custom kernel"},{"id":"p34s1","text":"Not because the trigram algorithm is novel. It isn't — Zoekt has done this well for years, and this "},{"id":"p34s2","text":"project measured itself against Zoekt on every accepted change."},{"id":"p35s1","text":"The reason is that buying the index means buying its process boundary, and the boundary costs more t"},{"id":"p35s2","text":"han the search. Here is where Zoekt's slowest query on the vite corpus actually spent its 18.32 ms:"},{"id":"p36s1","text":"| Stage | Time | Share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Zoekt's own search | 1.24 ms | 7% |
| HTTP transpor"},{"id":"p36s2","text":"t + JSON decode | 3.58 ms | 20% |
| Verification (mostly `rg` process startup) | 8.34 ms | 45% |
| L"},{"id":"p36s3","text":"ocal merge and classification | 5.14 ms | 28% |"},{"id":"p37s1","text":"**The search itself is 7% of the bill.** The other 93% is the cost of the index living somewhere els"},{"id":"p37s2","text":"e: serialise the query, cross a socket, decode JSON, then spawn ripgrep to re-read files the index a"},{"id":"p37s3","text":"lready had in memory. A single ripgrep spawn has a floor of about 6 ms on this machine — that alone "},{"id":"p37s4","text":"outweighs the entire search."},{"id":"p38s1","text":"Owning the kernel is what makes that 93% disappear:"},{"id":"p39s1","text":"- **The index is mapped into the agent's own memory.** No socket, no JSON, no serialisation. A query"},{"id":"p39s2","text":" is a function call.
- **Verification reads the mmap'd index, not the disk.** Candidates are confirm"},{"id":"p39s3","text":"ed in-process against bytes that are already resident, so there is no spawn and no second read.
- **"},{"id":"p39s4","text":"Unsupported queries can fail closed instead of approximating.** This one is not a performance argume"},{"id":"p39s5","text":"nt, and it is the reason a general-purpose library was not enough. An earlier attempt used an off-th"},{"id":"p39s6","text":"e-shelf file finder for candidate selection; on the Linux kernel tree it returned 17,767 files where"},{"id":"p39s7","text":" ripgrep found 17,772. Five missing files, from nested `.gitignore` re-inclusion rules — and a final"},{"id":"p39s8","text":" ripgrep pass can only remove extra results, never recover ones the candidate stage already dropped."},{"id":"p39s9","text":" When the recall boundary is someone else's implementation detail, you cannot prove it, and you cann"},{"id":"p39s10","text":"ot fix it.
- **The index format is tuned for this shape of data** — compressed content blocks, delta"},{"id":"p39s11","text":"-varint gram metadata — which is how the index lands at 0.38–0.91× the size of the source it indexes"},{"id":"p39s12","text":"varint gram metadata — which is how the index lands at 0.38–0.91× the size of the source it indexes."},{"id":"p40s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p41s1","text":"## How it works"},{"id":"p42s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p43s1","text":"1. 3. Verify exa"},{"id":"p43s3","text":"ctly, in-process, over the mmap'd index — no subprocess, no re-read from disk.

Materialize only t"},{"id":"p43s4","text":"he lines actually needed for the requested limit and context."},{"id":"p44s1","text":"The index is a single file per repository, built from a clean git snapshot, with content blocks comp"},{"id":"p44s2","text":"ressed and gram metadata delta-varint encoded."}],"truncated":true}
